findings.title: updateEvent fallback always returns undefined
findings.body: The new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is reached only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate searches for `cal.externalId === undefined`, which never matches. The previous behavior was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (a valid fallback). Now `selectedCalendar` is undefined when externalCalendarId is omitted, and there is no `'primary'` fallback like `createEvent` has — the update is sent to `calendarId: undefined`, which Google rejects. This breaks updates for any booking whose stored `externalCalendarId` is null (notably pre-refactor bookings created before references existed).

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback always returns undefined
findings.body: Same bug as in updateEvent: the find-against-undefined pattern guarantees no match, so `calendarId` falls back to 'primary' regardless of where the event actually lives. Result: deleteEvent targets a calendar that doesn't contain the event, returning 404, and the `if (err.code === 404) return resolve();` handler silently swallows the failure. Real deletion therefore never occurs for legacy bookings where `externalCalendarId` is null.

findings.title: TypeError when MeetLocationType has no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` produces `undefined` when the array is empty/absent. The very next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, which throws on `undefined`. Previously this was guarded by `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, so picking 'Google Meet' for any user without a destination calendar (a routine configuration) now 500s the booking instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation uses booking owner's credentials only
findings.body: Inside the recurring-event branch the code re-iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(c => c.type.endsWith('_calendar'))` rather than the credential already resolved for the current reference. For collective bookings the booking owner is only one of several hosts; the other hosts' calendar credentials live elsewhere in the database (the if-branch already handles this by falling back to `prisma.credential.findUnique`). Only using the owner's calendars means other hosts' recurring instances never get deleted. The inner loop should be driven by `updBooking.references`/`reference.credentialId`, not by the owner's credentials.

findings.title: Falls back to empty instead of user's destination calendar
findings.body: `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [...] : []` lost the user-level fallback present everywhere else. Every other handler in this PR (confirm, editLocation, handleCancelBooking, deleteCredential, paypal-webhook, stripe webhook) falls back to `user.destinationCalendar` when the booking has none. Pre-reschedule bookings with no destination calendar will now be sent through reschedule emails and reschedule webhooks with `destinationCalendar: []`, and EventManager then has no host calendar to invite, which can produce no calendar events for the requester.

findings.title: loadUsers refactor drops organization select
findings.body: The new `loadUsers` removed `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user branch. Any downstream code that reads the user's organization slug from the loaded user (including the post-load flow that may construct event URLs / emails / org-aware flows) will receive `undefined`. The original select surfaced organization data so removing it is a silent regression, not a cleanup.

findings.title: loadUsers error wrapping loses original status/context
findings.body: Any error (including the new dynamicUserList-empty check) is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users' unless it is already a Prisma error. This both changes observable behavior (a previously-silent empty dynamicUserList now turns into a 500 booking failure) and hides the real cause in logs. The empty-dynamicUserList guard should not be treated like a server failure.

findings.title: Inconsistent empty destinationCalendar value across handlers
findings.body: handleNewBooking emits `destinationCalendar: null` when both eventType and organizer have no destination calendar, while every other handler updated in this PR (confirm, editLocation, cancel, payment webhooks, deleteCredential, bookingReminder) emits `destinationCalendar: []` in the same case. Consumers (webhooks, emails, calendar services that do `[mainHost] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`) now have to handle both shapes for the same 'no calendar' semantic. Pick one (preferably `[]`) and apply it everywhere.

findings.title: Booking create no longer persists per-host references when result.externalId is missing
findings.body: In `create()` the new code sets `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId` for calendar references. The `else` branch in `createAllCalendarEvents` (when `destination.credentialId` is undefined) calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the third `externalId` argument, so `result.externalId` is undefined, and the new reference is created with an undefined `externalCalendarId`. Later updates/deletes on those references will not target any specific calendar and will fall back to 'primary' / fail. With the new multi-host flow this branch is also reachable for brand-new collective bookings if any destination entry lacks a credentialId.

findings.title: Unrelated logic change mixed into destinationCalendar PR
findings.body: The diff inverts the original `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` / `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug }` into ternaries. This is a real bug fix (the original logic put `slug` on the org when billing was disabled, which is almost certainly wrong) but it is completely unrelated to the destinationCalendar array migration. It is a maintainability concern: bundling behavioral fixes in unrelated PRs makes bisecting and reverting harder, and this PR does not document or test the new behavior.

findings.title: Booking-references loop runs delete logic serially before any awaits
findings.body: The outer `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` does multiple sequential awaits per iteration: a Prisma `findUnique` for the credential, then possibly another to get a calendar, then `deleteEvent`. With multiple calendar references (collective bookings), this serializes N round-trips before any deletes actually fire. The deleteEvent calls themselves are collected as promises and awaited together later (`Promise.allSettled(...apiDeletes)`), so they are parallel, but the credential/calendar lookups preceding them are not. For a 5-host collective this turns into 5 sequential DB reads per cancellation. Hoist `prisma.credential.findUnique` lookups into a `Promise.all` and only await `getCalendar` after, or cache by id.

findings.title: schedulingType added to CalendarEvent but unused
findings.body: A new `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` field is added to `CalendarEvent`, and `handleNewBooking.ts` writes it onto `evt`. No consumer in this diff (or elsewhere in the codebase per the changes shown) reads it, and there is no documentation explaining which calendar integrations are expected to key off it. It is purely dead surface area — either remove it until a consumer exists or commit the consumer together with this PR.
